title: Provision-to-ready automation sprint retro + follow-ups (action items + next sprint proposals)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Retro + follow-ups for the Provision-to-ready automation sprint. This issue is the canonical place for: (1) what shipped, (2) measured impact vs baseline, (3) incidents/pain points encountered during pilots, and (4) the follow-up backlog (action items + proposed next sprint work).

Context
- Sprint goal: reduce Dedicated pool time-to-ready by automating provisioning → imaging → bootstrap → validation → Ready handoff to routing.
- Pilot scope: 2 internal pools (staging + tooling) + 1 customer expansion window.

What shipped (this sprint)
1) State machine + orchestration
- Provisioning state model + persistence + audit trail (Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready/Failed)
  - github/redwood#48231
- API endpoints for triggering runs and querying status (authz + rate limiting)
  - github/redwood#48233
- Retry/backoff policy + safe cancellation semantics for imaging/bootstrap
  - github/redwood#48241
- Pause/resume and partial stage re-run (admin-only, audited)
  - github/redwood#48246, github/redwood#48247

2) IaC + bootstrap standardization
- Terraform module refactor for idempotent apply and standardized outputs
  - github/redwood-terraform#913, #914
- Helm chart pinning + provisioning bootstrap hooks
  - github/redwood-helm-charts#511

3) Validation & readiness gates
- Readiness gates: GPU health + DNS/TLS + runtime smoke test pass/fail with operator-friendly errors
  - ENG-2746; github/redwood#48242
- Perf-canary readiness suite integration (minimal benchmark mode + summary JSON)
  - github/perf-canary#287
- Correct Ready semantics: routing only advertises pools marked Ready (not Validating)
  - github/redwood#48234
- Fixed: prevent Ready from being set before perf-canary completion (transactional check)
  - github/redwood#48245

4) Config schema validation (with break-glass)
- Config schema + initial lint/policy rules with tests + example configs
  - github/redwood#48235, #48248
- Break-glass override w/ admin-only access + audit logs + alert hook
  - github/redwood#48236

5) Observability & comms
- Structured stage events with correlation IDs; plumbed to logs/metrics
  - github/redwood#48232
- Telemetry: time-to-ready histograms (overall + per-stage), error categorization w/ cardinality safeguards
  - github/redwood#48239
- Dashboards + alerts templates (stuck stage + elevated failure rate)
  - github/observability-pack#1204
- Slack bot status updates for #eng-infra (stage durations + failure summaries)
  - github/redwood#48240

Measured impact (baseline → pilot)
Source: backfilled logs for last 10 bring-ups + 3 pilot runs.
- Overall time-to-ready
  - Baseline (pre-sprint): p50 ~ 9.6 hours, p95 ~ 26 hours
  - Pilot (automation): p50 ~ 4.2 hours, p95 ~ 9.8 hours
- Stage improvements (largest wins)
  - Imaging: reduced variance via artifact mirror selection + retry/backoff; biggest remaining long-tail driver in 1 region.
  - Bootstrapping: fewer manual steps, but still a common failure mode when helm values drift/mismatch.
- Remaining long poles
  - Cloud quota/IAM friction for new pools in certain accounts/regions.
  - SKU heterogeneity (driver/toolkit assumptions) causing image + validation edge cases.

What went well
- Clear stage ownership + correlation IDs made triage materially faster (SRE + Infra both reported fewer “where is this stuck?” loops).
- Ready semantics clarified: routing consumption is now conservative and predictable; reduced risk of partial traffic during validation windows.
- Break-glass mechanism unblocked a legitimate edge-case during pilot without silently weakening policy gates.

What hurt / where we lost time
1) Bootstrapping failures due to helm values mismatch
- Incident-style event: runs stuck in Bootstrapping because a values override diverged from the pinned chart expectations.
- Outcome: better errors + runbook pointers landed, but root cause is still possible when teams hand-edit values.

2) Config validation false positives (edge cases)
- One pilot config was blocked due to a field combination not covered by initial schema migration guidance.
- We used break-glass, but the operator UX was still too “scary” and required too much human coordination.

3) IAM/quota failures are still noisy
- Terraform apply failures due to missing permissions/quotas created confusion: is this “infra problem” vs “pipeline problem” vs “account setup problem?”
- Paging policy was debated; we defaulted to tickets for non-urgent failures but need better categorization and ownership routing.

4) Slack bot duplicates and alert noise
- Duplicate stage updates created channel fatigue during the first staging run.
- Alert thresholds were adjusted, but we should formalize the “page vs ticket vs FYI” matrix for stuck stages.

Decisions captured
- Ready is a strict state: capacity is not usable by routing until perf-canary + validation complete.
- Manual overrides are allowed but must be:
  - admin-only,
  - audited,
  - time-bound (where possible),
  - surfaced on dashboard (so it’s never “silent”).

Action items / follow-ups (create/track as sub-issues)
ENG-2791 — Bootstrapping drift guardrails
- Owner: Nina Petrova
- Goal: prevent helm-values drift from causing stuck Bootstrapping; add diff + “known-safe” templates per pool type.
- Deliverable: preflight check that fails fast with explicit remediation.

ENG-2792 — Config validation migration helper + allowlist policy
- Owner: Benji Okafor
- Goal: reduce break-glass usage by providing a migration tool and a temporary audited allowlist for known legacy configs.

ENG-2793 — IAM/quota error taxonomy + ownership routing
- Owner: Rafael Mendes
- Goal: map common Terraform/IAM/quota failures to a clear owner (Infra vs CloudOps vs SRE) and to an action (auto-retry, ticket, page).

ENG-2794 — Imaging step long-tail mitigation (regional mirrors/prewarm)
- Owner: Victor Alvarez
- Goal: implement detection + fallback mirror selection and prewarm strategy for the region/SKU that timeouts.

ENG-2795 — Tighten “stuck stage” alerts + noise budget
- Owner: Aisha Bello
- Goal: finalize thresholds (page vs ticket) and document; align with SLO reporting cadence.

ENG-2796 — Operator UX pass on CLI (flags + errors + links)
- Owner: Vanessa Ortiz
- Goal: incorporate feedback from operators: clearer stage rerun semantics, better dry-run outputs, and consistent links to dashboards/runbooks.

ENG-2797 — Control plane “Ready” API compatibility + deprecation plan
- Owner: Ethan Park
- Goal: confirm backward compatibility with existing pool registration flows; define deprecation timeline for any legacy fields.

ENG-2798 — Perf-canary thresholds per SKU + region defaults
- Owner: Rina Kobayashi
- Goal: codify thresholds so we don’t treat minor SKU variance as a hard failure; implement per-SKU baselines with safe defaults.

ENG-2799 — Signed artifact provenance verification for golden images (next step)
- Owner: Marcus Lin
- Goal: extend image provenance checks to runtime bootstrap (verify signatures/attestations during imaging/bootstrap, not just build time).

ENG-2800 — Quarterly “time-to-ready” report template + exec visibility
- Owner: Jamal Pierce
- Goal: create a lightweight recurring report (p50/p95 by region/SKU, top failure modes, automation adoption rate).

Next sprint proposals (bundle candidates)
1) “Drift + Guardrails” sprintlet
- Focus: drift detection + preflight checks + reducing Bootstrapping failures.
- Proposed success metric: cut Bootstrapping-related failures by 50% and reduce p95 by ~2h.

2) “Operator Experience” sprintlet
- Focus: CLI UX, runbooks, and alerting/paging hygiene.
- Proposed success metric: reduce operator interventions per run; reduce duplicate/low-signal Slack notifications.

3) “Policy Hardening” sprintlet
- Focus: config validation migration + allowlist controls; better break-glass ergonomics.
- Proposed success metric: break-glass usage < 5% of runs, with zero silent overrides.
